title: When AI Gives the Answer, Who Does the Learning?
subtitle: AI 給了答案，那學習的是誰？
source: 原創議題文章；研究內容依 Bastani et al.（PNAS, 2025）原文與 Kosmyna et al.（arXiv 預印本, 2025）摘要，2026-10-22 核對

sources.title: Bastani, H. et al. (2025). Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics. PNAS 122(26).
Kosmyna, N. et al. (2025). Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing Task. arXiv:2506.08872 (preprint).
Plutarch, On Listening to Lectures (Moralia, Loeb ed., 1927), via LacusCurtius

beginner.title: Help Now, Harder Later?
paras: Many students now use AI chatbots for homework. You type a question, and a few seconds later you get a clear answer. It feels very helpful. But here is a question: when the AI does the work, are you still learning?
現在很多學生用 AI 聊天機器人寫作業。你打一個問題，幾秒後就得到清楚的答案，感覺非常有幫助。但有個問題：當 AI 幫你做完功課，你還在學習嗎？

Researchers tested this in a big high school in Turkey. Nearly 1,000 students did math practice in class. Some students used a normal chatbot, like ChatGPT. Some used a special “AI tutor”. Others used no AI at all. After the practice, everyone took a test without any help. The math topics were ones they had already studied.
研究人員在土耳其一所大型高中測試了這個問題。將近一千名學生在課堂上做數學練習。有些學生用一般的聊天機器人，像 ChatGPT；有些用特別設計的「AI 家教」；其他人完全不用 AI。練習結束後，每個人都在沒有任何協助的情況下參加考試。這些數學主題是他們之前已經學過的。

During practice, the AI groups did much better. Students with the normal chatbot scored 48% higher than students with no AI. But on the test, the normal chatbot group did worse — 17% lower than the students who never used AI. Many of them had simply asked for answers and copied them.
練習時，用 AI 的組別表現好很多。用一般聊天機器人的學生，分數比沒用 AI 的學生高了 48%。但到了考試，一般聊天機器人組反而表現更差——比從沒用過 AI 的學生低了 17%。他們很多人只是要答案，然後照抄。

The AI tutor group was different. Their tutor gave help but was designed to protect learning, and students used it to ask for help and try answers themselves. On the test, they did about as well as the students with no AI. Interestingly, the students who copied answers did not think they had learned less.
AI 家教組就不一樣了。他們的家教會提供協助，但設計上是為了保護學習，學生用它來求助，並自己嘗試作答。考試時，他們的表現和沒用 AI 的學生差不多。有意思的是，那些照抄答案的學生，並不覺得自己學得比較少。

So AI is not good or bad by itself. It depends on how we use it. If AI thinks for us, our brains do less work, and we learn less. If AI helps us think, it can be useful. Try this: write your own answer first, and then ask AI to check it.
所以 AI 本身沒有好壞之分，要看我們怎麼用它。如果 AI 替我們思考，我們的大腦就做得比較少，學到的也比較少。如果 AI 幫助我們思考，它就很有用。試試看：先寫下你自己的答案，再請 AI 幫你檢查。

intermediate.title: When AI Gives the Answer, Who Does the Learning?
paras: Generative AI can now solve a maths problem, summarise a chapter or draft an essay in seconds. For students, the temptation is obvious. But there is a difference between completing a task and learning from it. If a chatbot does the thinking, does the student still build the skill — or only the appearance of one?
生成式 AI 現在可以在幾秒內解出數學題、摘要一章課文，或寫出一篇文章草稿。對學生來說，誘惑顯而易見。但完成一項任務和從中學到東西，是兩回事。如果聊天機器人替學生思考，學生還能培養出能力嗎——還是只培養出能力的假象？

A large experiment published in 2025 offers one answer. Researchers worked with a high school in Turkey, where nearly 1,000 students in about fifty classes took part in four 90-minute maths sessions. Students were randomly given one of three conditions: a standard chatbot based on GPT-4 (“GPT Base”), a version with guardrails designed with teachers’ input (“GPT Tutor”), or no AI. Afterwards, all students took an exam on their own. Each session followed the same pattern: a teacher first reviewed a topic, such as combinatorics, then students practised, and finally they took a test. During practice, every group could also use their notes and textbook.

2025 年發表的一項大型實驗提供了一個答案。研究人員與土耳其一所高中合作，約五十個班、將近一千名學生參加了四次各 90 分鐘的數學課程。學生被隨機分配到三種情況之一：以 GPT-4 為基礎的一般聊天機器人（GPT Base）、依教師意見設計防護機制的版本（GPT Tutor），或完全不用 AI。之後，所有學生都獨自參加考試。每次課程都依照同樣的流程：老師先複習一個主題，例如排列組合，接著學生練習，最後考試。練習時，每一組也都可以使用筆記和課本。

During practice, AI made a big difference: compared with the no-AI group, scores rose by 48% with GPT Base and by 127% with GPT Tutor. The exam told a different story. Students who had used GPT Base scored 17% lower than those who had never had access. An analysis of their chats showed that many had used it as a “crutch”, asking for solutions and copying them.
練習期間，AI 造成了很大的差異：和沒用 AI 的組相比，GPT Base 組分數提高了 48%，GPT Tutor 組提高了 127%。考試卻是另一回事。用過 GPT Base 的學生，分數比從未使用過的學生低了 17%。對話紀錄分析顯示，很多人把它當成「拐杖」，直接要解答然後照抄。

GPT Tutor students, by contrast, used the tool to ask for help and attempt answers independently. Their harmful effect essentially disappeared, though they did not do better than the control group either. Perhaps most worrying, students who copied solutions did not believe they had learned less. The tool made them feel more capable than they were.
相較之下，GPT Tutor 組的學生用這個工具來求助，並自己嘗試作答。他們的負面效果基本上消失了，不過也沒有比對照組表現得更好。最令人擔憂的或許是：照抄解答的學生，並不認為自己學得比較少。這個工具讓他們覺得自己比實際上更有能力。

The lesson is not that students should avoid AI, but that design and habits matter. A tool that hands over answers removes the effort that learning requires. A tool — or a student — that keeps the thinking on the human side can turn AI into a coach rather than a substitute. One practical habit: attempt the problem first, then use AI to check your reasoning, not to replace it.
這個教訓不是學生應該避開 AI，而是設計與習慣很重要。直接交出答案的工具，拿走了學習所需要的努力。而一個讓思考留在人這一邊的工具——或學生——可以把 AI 變成教練，而不是替身。一個實用的習慣是：先自己嘗試解題，再用 AI 檢查你的推理，而不是取代它。

advanced.title: Performance, Learning and the Crutch Problem
paras: Few technologies have entered classrooms as quickly as generative AI. A chatbot can now produce a worked solution, a summary or a polished paragraph faster than most students can read the question. Much of the public debate has focused on cheating. A more fundamental question concerns learning itself: if a tool improves what students produce, does it also improve what they can do once the tool is gone?
很少有技術像生成式 AI 這樣迅速進入教室。聊天機器人現在產出完整解題、摘要或潤飾過的段落的速度，比大多數學生讀完題目還快。公眾辯論多半聚焦在作弊上。一個更根本的問題，關乎學習本身：如果一個工具改善了學生的產出，它是否也改善了學生在沒有這個工具之後的能力？

A preregistered field experiment published in PNAS in 2025 addressed exactly this distinction. Working with a large high school in Turkey during the 2023–2024 school year, researchers ran four 90-minute maths sessions for about fifty classes, comprising nearly 1,000 students. Students were randomly assigned to one of three arms: GPT Base, which mimicked a standard ChatGPT interface; GPT Tutor, built on the same model but with guardrails designed from teacher input; or no AI. Each session followed three stages: a teacher’s review of a previously taught topic, an assisted practice period in which all students also had their notes and textbook, and finally an unassisted exam.

2025 年發表於《美國國家科學院院刊》（PNAS）的一項事先登記的田野實驗，正面處理了這個區別。研究人員在 2023–2024 學年與土耳其一所大型高中合作，為約五十個班、將近一千名學生進行了四次 90 分鐘的數學課程。學生被隨機分配到三組之一：模仿一般 ChatGPT 介面的 GPT Base；以同一模型打造、但依教師意見加入防護機制的 GPT Tutor；或不使用 AI。每次課程分三個階段：老師複習先前教過的主題；有輔助的練習時段，所有學生也都可以使用筆記和課本；最後是無輔助的考試。

The results separate performance from learning with unusual clarity. On practice problems, GPT Base raised scores by 48% relative to the control group, and GPT Tutor by 127%. On the unassisted exam, however, GPT Base students scored 17% lower than students who had never had access. The guardrails in GPT Tutor essentially eliminated this harm, although they produced no measurable gain. Interaction logs explained the pattern: GPT Base was frequently used as a “crutch” to request and copy solutions, whereas GPT Tutor prompted more substantive use, such as asking for help or attempting answers independently.

這些結果以少見的清晰度，把「表現」和「學習」區分開來。在練習題上，GPT Base 讓分數比對照組提高了 48%，GPT Tutor 提高了 127%。然而在無輔助的考試中，GPT Base 組的學生比從未使用過的學生低了 17%。GPT Tutor 的防護機制基本上消除了這種傷害，雖然沒有帶來可測量的進步。互動紀錄解釋了這個模式：GPT Base 經常被當作「拐杖」，用來索取並照抄解答；GPT Tutor 則促成更實質的使用，例如求助或自己嘗試作答。

Perhaps the most troubling finding concerns self-perception. Students who had leaned on GPT Base did not perceive that they had learned less or performed worse, and GPT Tutor students believed they had done significantly better than they actually had. This mismatch echoes a familiar problem in learning research: fluent, effortless experiences feel like progress even when little is retained. A preliminary MIT study, released as a preprint and involving only 54 participants, points in a similar direction: people who wrote essays with an AI assistant showed the weakest brain connectivity and struggled to quote their own work.

最令人不安的發現，或許與自我認知有關。依賴 GPT Base 的學生，並不覺得自己學得較少或表現較差；GPT Tutor 組的學生則認為自己表現得比實際上好得多。這種落差呼應了學習研究中一個常見的問題：流暢、不費力的經驗，即使幾乎沒留下什麼，也會讓人感覺在進步。一項麻省理工學院的初步研究（以預印本發表，只有 54 名參與者）也指向類似方向：用 AI 助手寫作文的人，大腦連結最弱，而且難以準確引用自己寫的內容。

None of this implies that AI should be banned from schools. The same model produced very different outcomes depending on how it was designed and used. The deeper principle is that learning requires the learner to do the cognitive work: to retrieve, to struggle, to make and correct mistakes. Tools that remove that effort optimise for the wrong outcome. The challenge for teachers and students alike is to use AI in ways that keep the thinking — and the responsibility for it — firmly on the human side.
這一切並不代表應該在學校禁用 AI。同一個模型，因為設計與使用方式不同，產生了截然不同的結果。更深層的原則是：學習需要學習者自己做認知工作——提取、掙扎、犯錯再修正。拿走這些努力的工具，是在為錯誤的目標做最佳化。對老師和學生而言，挑戰都在於：以能讓思考——以及思考的責任——牢牢留在人這一邊的方式使用 AI。
